title: Unused Type Parameters (Speculative Generics)
pattern: Structs or methods that declare type parameters that are never bound or used in active execution or validation logic, represented only in `PhantomData` fields.
why_bad: It forces all downstream call sites to specify dummy type arguments, making API usage highly repetitive and verbose without any type-checking benefit.
detection: A type parameter declared on a struct that is only used in a `PhantomData` field and is never constrained or utilized in any field values or method bounds.
counterexample: Typing parameters that enforce strict compile-time state machines or type-safe session types.
fix: Remove the generic type parameter and the `PhantomData` marker.
source: Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages* (2002), Chapter 19; Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3 ("Speculative Generality").
